description:
An adversarial review of the cross-surface SQL<->DataFrame equivalence campaign
(PRs #826-#848 on develop) reproduced every finding by running the gates and
found the oracle is real but narrow, oversold, and partly vacuous. This TODO
addresses ALL of those findings. The committed evidence the review draws on
lives in _project/analysis/clickbench-cross-surface-divergences.md,
_project/analysis/joinorder-synthetic-cross-surface-divergences.md, and
_project/analysis/oracle-coverage-map.md; reproduce any cell with
`make <benchmark>-cross-surface-equivalence-report`.

The headline problem: PR #848 concluded "ClickBench has ~no genuine DataFrame
logic bugs" and triaged 27 divergences as "tie-ambiguous top-N." That is false.
Re-running the gate shows at least three REAL, deterministic DataFrame bugs that
#848 rationalized away as ties:
  - Q6_pandas: wrong COUNT(DISTINCT SearchPhrase) (18 SQL vs 17 pandas), a
    scalar with NO ORDER BY and NO LIMIT - a tie is impossible. Root cause: the
    DataFrame loader maps empty-string -> None and pandas .nunique() drops the
    null. SearchPhrase has 74,724 empty strings / 0 nulls.
  - Q17_pandas / Q18_pandas: wrong GROUP BY - pandas default groupby(dropna=True)
    silently drops ~74k null-key rows, so the query runs over ~25% of the data.
    The count multiset differs, which a boundary tie cannot cause.
  - Q24 / Q17 col-1 "" vs None: the SAME root cause #848 deferred as a cosmetic
    "dtype" issue. It is not cosmetic - it changes COUNT(DISTINCT) and GROUP BY
    membership.

Compounding issues the review proved by reproduction:
  - NON-DETERMINISM: the ClickBench gate returned 27 -> 25 -> 26 divergent cells
    across three identical runs, with per-query values changing run to run. The
    generated DATA is byte-identical across runs (verified by md5), so the wobble
    is ENGINE tie-ordering (DuckDB/Polars thread parallelism under
    LIMIT-without-total-ORDER), NOT data. random.seed(42) cannot fix it, and a
    known_divergences baseline is therefore un-pinnable.
  - ORDER-BY BLINDNESS: ResultValidator.validate_results_exact sorts FULL ROWS
    before comparing (tpchavoc/validation.py:54-79), so ORDER BY is never checked
    except via which rows survive LIMIT. A reversed ORDER BY passes silently;
    equally-valid tie picks are flagged as false divergences; a column mixing
    None and non-None crashes Python sorted() and is mislabeled "error:".
  - VACUOUS CELLS: at SF=0.1, 6 of 13 SSB queries (Q2.1-2.3, Q3.3, Q3.4, Q4.3)
    return ZERO rows on both surfaces, so 12 of 26 SSB cells pass empty-vs-empty
    while the report counts them as "compared". The build guards empty TABLES
    (cross_surface.py:261) but not empty RESULTS.
  - FALSE INDEPENDENCE: SSB and ~40/43 ClickBench DataFrame queries are GENERATED
    from a compact DSL spec, and BOTH "independent backends" are emitted from the
    SAME spec row - so a spec-level logic error appears identically on both, and
    the docs' "two independent implementations" claim (cross_surface.py:3-6,
    dataframe_surface.py:48-50) is false for them. CoffeeShop (hand-written) is
    the genuine exception.
  - LOADER BYPASS: the gate materializes contexts straight from typed DuckDB
    Arrow (dataframe_surface.py:74-125), never through DataFrameDataLoader, so a
    green gate proves NOTHING about the production CSV->parquet loader's dtype
    fidelity (leading-zero VARCHAR->int, empty->null). #847 "deferred dtype" is
    docs-only and the bug is still live; the #846 DDL parser is a naive
    whitespace tokenizer that breaks on DECIMAL(p, s), quoted names, and
    multi-word types.
  - GOVERNANCE: STAGED gates are not run in CI and have no promotion forcing
    function; "guarded" in the coverage map means "registered in the GATES dict",
    not "verified green"; the "12 gateable" applicability headline counts 6
    benchmarks whose SQL<->DF id mapping was never verified (the team's own TODO
    says "do NOT guess").

anti_patterns.dont: count an empty-vs-empty or unverified-id-mapping cell as coverage
anti_patterns.why: that is the exact 'theater' the review flagged.

anti_patterns.dont: fix the null bug only in the gate path or only in the generated factories
anti_patterns.instead: fix the loader contract (w1) and verify on the real run path.
anti_patterns.why: production and hand-written impls would stay broken

anti_patterns.instead: extend it with an opt-in order/tie-aware mode.

anti_patterns.dont: promote a staged gate to GATES while it is nondeterministic or has a non-empty baseline
anti_patterns.why: GATES membership is the coverage signal

anti_patterns.dont: silence a divergence by adding it to known_divergences
anti_patterns.instead: fix the wrong surface (this is exactly how #848 went wrong).
anti_patterns.why: the baseline is for intentional presentational differences only

deferrals.reason: Large; cross-surface proves agreement not correctness. Tracked as a deeper question in the review, not required to close these findings.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] duplicate: Independent SQL oracle for non-tpch/tpcds benchmarks is owned by active benchmark-correctness-oracle-coverage-map ('small curated expected-results subset') and cross-surface-gate-rollout-followups w2 fallback oracle.
deferrals.summary: A truly independent SQL-side oracle for non-tpch/tpcds benchmarks (e.g. upstream published answer sets).

deferrals.reason: Additive enhancement beyond w6's acceptance and M4's core concern (which is resolved: the gate drives the real production loader and already caught the TEXT->null / TIMESTAMP->string dtype bugs via value comparison). Designing an acceptable cross-engine dtype-equivalence map is a separable piece.
deferrals.summary: A dedicated DTYPE-asserting cross-surface gate cell (compare each loaded column's dtype, not just its values, against the SQL reference).

deferrals.reason: A separate SSB data-generation bug, not a cross-surface oracle defect; the vacuous cells are honestly classified in the ssb gate's allowlist. Tracked in #870.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] obsolete: Fixed: benchbox/core/ssb/generator.py:567 emits canonical 2-digit MFGR#12; DONE item ssb-generator-p-category-bug.yaml (Completed) + test_ssb_cross_surface_equivalence.py:89-98 pins the six queries non-empty. Allowlist removed.
deferrals.summary: SSB generator emits a 3-digit p_category ('MFGR#212') so the standard SSB Q2.x predicates ('MFGR#12') match no rows at any scale (Q2.1-2.3/Q3.3/Q3.4/Q4.3 empty to SF=1.0).

preserves.behavior: All TPC-Havoc SQL and DataFrame equivalence gates stay green with empty baselines and byte-identical output - the comparator change (w2) is additive, never a fork.
SSB and CoffeeShop enforced gates stay green throughout (CoffeeShop is the reference 'good' gate).
The bounded one-cell-per-benchmark cost model is preserved; no full platform matrix in routine PRs.

benchbox run default (execution-only) behavior is unchanged for every benchmark; gate and loader changes must keep the real DataFrame run path working (re-verify a DataFrame benchmark run after w1/w6).

verifications.command: python -m benchbox.core.equivalence.cross_surface --benchmark clickbench  (x3, expect identical deterministic output)
verifications.description: Re-run the full review reproduction appendix and confirm each finding is resolved.

verifications.command: pytest tests for cross-surface mutation sensitivity (w10)
verifications.description: Mutation tests prove the gate catches seeded filter/group/sort/join bugs.

work_units.notes:
The DataFrame surface conflates SQL '' with None, which changes results, not
just presentation. Two layers must be decided and fixed:

ROOT FIX (preferred) - loader fidelity: a CSV empty field in a declared
string/VARCHAR/TEXT column must materialize as '' (matching DuckDB/SQL), not
Arrow null. Today convert_csv_to_parquet passes strings_can_be_null=True
(data_loader.py:329) and pandas read_csv uses default na_values, so empties
become null on the production path; the gate path (DuckDB->Arrow) keeps ''.
Decide the canonical contract (recommend: declared-string empties stay '',
matching the SQL reference and the upstream ClickBench data) and enforce it on
BOTH load paths. This is the true fix and also resolves Q24/Q17-col1.

SYMPTOM FIX (only if the loader contract cannot be '' for a real reason):
make the generated factories null-correct - groupby(..., dropna=False) in
_make_group_pandas (clickbench queries.py:291; mirror in ssb) and a
null-aware distinct count instead of bare pandas .nunique() (queries.py:206/
285). But note this only patches generated factories; hand-written impls and
future benchmarks would still be exposed - which is why the loader fix is
preferred.

Whichever path: verify against the REAL DataFrame run (dataframe_runner /
benchmark_mixin), not the gate only - the gate bypasses the loader (see w6),
so a gate-only fix would be invisible to production.
work_units.summary: Fix the empty-string/null conflation in the DataFrame load path (C1: Q6, Q17, Q18, Q24 are REAL bugs)

work_units.notes:
The campaign measured only that the gates PASS (specificity); it never measured
whether they CATCH a seeded bug (sensitivity). Add a mutation-test harness that,
per gated benchmark, injects a known DataFrame error and asserts the gate goes
RED:
  - flip a filter comparator (< -> <=),
  - drop a GROUP BY key,
  - reverse a sort direction (this is the BS2 regression guard),
  - drop a join.
For each mutation that the gate does NOT catch, document why (e.g. an empty-
result query from BS3, or an order-only change the comparator ignores) and feed
it back into w2/w4. This closes the central unanswered question: is the oracle
strong enough to find logic bugs, or did it find "no bugs" because it is too
weak/vacuous?
work_units.summary: Mutation-test the oracle to measure SENSITIVITY, not just specificity (C2 - the central question)

work_units.notes:
validate_results_exact (validation.py:54-79) sorts full rows then compares
positionally, so it is simultaneously BLIND to real ORDER BY bugs (a reversed
order passes - DEMO1) and NOISY on legitimate ties (two equally-valid tie
picks fail - DEMO2), and it crashes on a column mixing None with non-None
because Python sorted() cannot order None vs int (DEMO3), which
find_surface_divergences (dataframe_surface.py:234) then mislabels as
"error:" instead of a clean result.

Add an ORDER-AWARE comparison mode for queries that declare an ORDER BY:
  - compare the ordered prefix up to the first tie group exactly (this
    restores ORDER BY signal), then
  - treat the rows sharing the boundary order-key as a MULTISET (this removes
    the tie noise that #848 mistook for the whole story).
For queries with no ORDER BY, keep multiset/set comparison.
Fix the sort key to place None deterministically (e.g. sort on a (is_none,
value) surrogate) so a NULL-bearing column never raises, and so a genuine
None-vs-value difference is reported as a MISMATCH, not an "error:".

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: this comparator is shared with the TPC-Havoc SQL and
DataFrame gates, which rely on its current semantics and run with empty
baselines. The order/tie-awareness must be additive (opt-in per query/gate)
and MUST keep all TPC-Havoc gates byte-identical-green. Do NOT fork the
validator for cross-surface only; extend it.
work_units.summary: Make the comparator order-aware and tie-aware; fix the None/NaN sort crash (BS2)

work_units.notes:
The wobble is engine tie-ordering, not data. Pin it at the gate:
  - run the gate's DuckDB connection and the Polars/pandas execution
    single-threaded (PRAGMA threads=1; pl.Config / POLARS_MAX_THREADS=1), AND
  - have both surfaces apply a deterministic TOTAL-ORDER tie-breaker before any
    LIMIT (append all remaining columns / a stable key to ORDER BY on the SQL
    reference and the DataFrame impls), so LIMIT truncation is reproducible.
Document explicitly (in cross_surface.py and the review's "determinism" claim)
that random.seed(42) makes the DATA reproducible but does NOT make the GATE
deterministic; the tie-breaker + single-thread is what does.
work_units.summary: Eliminate engine nondeterminism at the gate boundary (H1)

work_units.notes:
6/13 SSB queries return 0 rows at SF=0.1, so 12/26 cells pass empty-vs-empty.
Two parts:
  1. Gate hygiene: track per-query reference row count in
     find_cross_surface_divergences; in _report, count a both-empty cell as
     NON-discriminating. The gate should FAIL (or require an explicit
     classified "legitimately-empty" entry) if any gated query's reference is
     empty, and the "compared N of M cells" line must exclude vacuous cells
     from the discriminating count.
  2. Data discrimination: for SSB, choose query parameters (or a per-benchmark
     SF) so Q2.1-2.3/Q3.3/Q3.4/Q4.3 return rows at the bounded cell. Prefer
     parameterization over raising SF globally (keep PRs cheap).
Apply the same empty-result audit to coffeeshop (currently 0/11 empty - good),
clickbench, and joinorder_synthetic before promotion.
work_units.summary: Fail (not silently pass) on vacuous empty-vs-empty cells; make every gated query discriminating (BS3)

work_units.notes:
After w1 (null fix), w2 (tie-aware), w3 (determinism): re-run the ClickBench
gate. Expectation: the genuine ties (Q9, Q15, Q16, Q31, Q32, Q33, Q38) become
clean (tie-aware comparison), and the real bugs (Q6, Q17, Q18, Q24) are fixed
by w1. ANY residual divergence is a real bug to fix, verified by checking the
ORDER-BY-key multiset, not extrapolated.
Correct _project/analysis/clickbench-cross-surface-divergences.md: the "~no
genuine DataFrame logic bugs" conclusion was wrong; record that Q6/Q17/Q18
were real null-handling bugs sharing root cause with the deferred '' vs None
issue. Promote clickbench from STAGED_GATES to GATES only once it is green with
an empty baseline AND deterministic.
work_units.summary: Re-triage ClickBench with the fixed loader+comparator and correct the #848 record (C1 closeout)

work_units.notes:
The gate's loader bypass (dataframe_surface.py:74-125 materializes from typed
DuckDB Arrow) means it cannot see production CSV->parquet dtype corruption.
  - Add a gate cell/mode that loads each gated benchmark through the REAL
    DataFrameDataLoader (CSV->parquet->read_parquet) and compares both dtypes
    and values to the SQL reference, so loader corruption is observable.
  - Carry the w1 empty-string->'' contract to the remaining raw-CSV adapters.
    w1 fixed the Parquet path (strings_can_be_null=False) and the pandas CSV
    path; Polars scan_csv / modin / dask / cudf still map an empty string
    field to null on their raw-CSV read, so prefer_parquet=False (or a
    CSV-recommending adapter) reintroduces the Q6/Q17/Q18 divergence on those
    surfaces. Thread declared column types into each adapter's read_csv and
    preserve '' for string columns, mirroring pandas_df.read_csv.
  - Harden schema_utils.column_name/column_sql_type (schema_utils.py:29-51):
    replace the naive column.split() with a paren-aware, quote-aware DDL
    column parser that handles DECIMAL(10, 2) (space after comma), quoted/
    spaced names, and multi-word types (DOUBLE PRECISION, TIMESTAMP WITH TIME
    ZONE, NOT NULL DEFAULT ...). Add unit tests for each shape.
  - Extend PYARROW_TYPE_MAP and the polars/pandas maps (data_loader.py:191-199)
    to cover TEXT, BIGINT, REAL, DOUBLE PRECISION, NUMERIC, BOOLEAN so declared
    string/numeric types are applied at conversion instead of inferred.
  - Apply declared STRING dtypes on the production load path (not just date-
    name suppression) so a leading-zero VARCHAR is not inferred as int.
Re-verify the real DataFrame benchmark run still works (this is a loader fix,
not gate-only special-casing).
work_units.summary: Add a production-loader-path gate cell + harden the DDL parser and type maps (M4, L1, L2)

work_units.notes:
Correct the docstrings that assert "two independent implementations"
(cross_surface.py:3-6) and "independent ... can diverge independently"
(dataframe_surface.py:48-50). For SSB and ~40/43 ClickBench queries BOTH
backends are generated from one DSL spec row, so they cannot diverge on logic
- only on engine semantics; the only real independence is SQL-text vs DSL-spec
(same author, same understanding). State plainly that the oracle catches
TRANSCRIPTION errors, not CONCEPTUAL ones, for DSL-generated benchmarks.
Record per gated benchmark whether its DataFrame surface is hand-written
(coffeeshop) or generated (ssb, clickbench). Optional but recommended: for at
least the enforced gates, ensure one surface is independently authored, or add
a second independent reference (e.g. the upstream published ClickBench answer
set) so the oracle is not just self-consistency.
work_units.summary: Stop overclaiming independence; document what the oracle actually proves (BS1)

work_units.notes:
STAGED_GATES (clickbench, joinorder_synthetic) are not run in CI (pr.yml runs
only ssb + coffeeshop) and nothing fails when a staged gate is parked
indefinitely; test_clickbench_is_staged_not_enforced only BLESSES parking.
  - Add the staged cross-surface reports to a non-blocking CI job so their
    divergence snapshots cannot silently rot (promote to blocking once green
    via w5).
  - Add a governance test: a benchmark may sit in STAGED_GATES only with a
    dated rationale and an owner; fail if a staged gate has been parked past a
    declared review-by date. Delete a staged gate that no one will burn down
    rather than leave a permanent red parking lot.
work_units.summary: Run staged gates in CI and add a promotion forcing-function (M3)

work_units.notes:
- generate_oracle_coverage_map.py derives 'guarded' from GATES dict membership
  (85/111) and never checks the gate is green. Either run each gate (or read
  its CI result) and add a distinct 'verified-green' signal, or rename
  'guarded' -> 'gate-registered' so a registered-but-unverified gate is not
  reported as coverage.
- cross_surface_applicability_sweep.py counts 6 'needs-id-mapping' benchmarks
  (amplab, datavault, nyctaxi, tpcds_obt, tpch_skew, tsbs_devops) as 'gateable'
  on ZERO verified id overlap; the campaign's own TODO warns 'do NOT guess'
  the nyctaxi/tsbs mappings and tpcds_obt is 3 DF queries vs 89 SQL. Downgrade
  these from 'gateable' to 'candidate-unverified' until an independent
  SQL<->DF id mapping is confirmed per benchmark.
